# Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) computes a shared
balance-statistics schema for **bot** runs, but nothing aggregates the **same
statistics from human player games**. Today `npm run record` (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ)
captures raw dev-mode telemetry for a single human session, and
`npm run evaluate -- --human` does a same-seed metric comparison — but neither
produces the shared `BalanceStats` schema, so the bot cannot be validated as a
realistic proxy for a human player.

## Users

- **As a maintainer**, I want to record a human play session in dev mode and get
  the same balance statistics the bot framework produces, so I can compare the
  bot's experience against a real player's and validate that the bot is a
  realistic proxy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A **single shared pure helper** (consumed by both `npm run record` and
   `npm run evaluate -- --human`) converts a recorded human session's telemetry
   record stream into per-run `BalanceRunStats` (one per `run_header`) plus a
   `BalanceAggregate`, reusing `extractBalanceStats` and
   `aggregateBalanceStats`/`createBalanceAggregator` from the automated-balancing
   framework — no schema duplication (the shared `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`
   is used).
2. The human statistics artifact **reuses the existing `BalanceReport` shape**
   (`kind: 'balance'`) via `buildBalanceReport`, labelled with a `human`
   pseudo-policy so bot and human reports are directly comparable.
3. **Dev mode only.** Collection exists only in the dev tooling
   (`scripts/record-session.mjs` / `scripts/evaluate.mjs`); there is no change to
   production telemetry/consent config and no new production call site. No PII is
   recorded or emitted — the artifact contains only schema fields (numeric stats,
   seeds, archetype/upgrade keys, hashes).
4. When a recording contains **multiple human runs**, every run yields a per-run
   `BalanceRunStats` entry **and** one aggregate across all runs, mirroring the
   bot batch output. Output is deterministic (stable serialisation).
5. Tests cover the pure helper (single run, multiple runs, empty stream, seed
   attribution, determinism) and both tool paths (record emits the artifact,
   evaluate `--human` emits it under `--out`); a test asserts no production
   call site collects via the new path (dev-only enforcement).
6. Documentation updated (`docs/TELEMETRY.md` recording section and/or
   `docs/BALANCING.md` statistics section describe the human flow and artifact);
   full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the dev-mode recording path (`run_header` / `tick` / `event` records) — no new recording mechanism.
- Reuse the shared balance-statistics schema — same code path, not a divergent copy.
- Dev-tooling only: production telemetry/consent unchanged, no PII.
- The dev tools load the TS core via Vite SSR (as `scripts/evaluate.mjs` already does).
- Artifact shape reuses `BalanceReport` (`kind: 'balance'`, `policy: 'human'`).
- Human tickets are sampled (`sampleEveryTicks`); survival-time derivation uses
  tick numbers with the default `dtSeconds` (1/60) — report `ticks`/`dt` config
  fields are derived accordingly.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — `extractBalanceStats(records)` / `aggregateBalanceStats(points)` (pure, clock-free).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — `buildBalanceReport` / `BalanceReport` / `serialiseReport` / `fnv1aHash`.
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — `npm run record`: human session → JSONL via telemetry sink.
- `scripts/recording.mjs` — `parseRecording` splits a recording into per-run ticks/events.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — `--human` does a same-seed metric comparison (not balance stats).
- `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — `parseTelemetryJsonl` for the dev sink's flat record stream.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure helper (in `src/ai/eval/`, exported from the eval index) that
   splits a flat telemetry record stream at `run_header` boundaries and reduces
   each run through `extractBalanceStats`, aggregates via
   `aggregateBalanceStats`, and packages a `BalanceReport` (via
   `buildBalanceReport`) with `policy: 'human'`.
2. Wire `scripts/record-session.mjs` to write a `balance-stats.json` artifact
   next to the recording (or under `--out`) by loading the TS core via Vite SSR.
3. Wire `scripts/evaluate.mjs --human` to emit the same `human` `BalanceReport`
   artifact under `--out` (a pure shell over the shared helper).
4. Document the human flow + artifact in `docs/TELEMETRY.md` / `docs/BALANCING.md`.
5. Unit-test the pure helper and both tool paths; assert dev-only enforcement.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — reuse `extractBalanceStats` / `aggregateBalanceStats` (no change expected; source of the schema).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — reuse `buildBalanceReport` / `BalanceReport` (no change expected).
- `src/ai/eval/` (new pure helper, e.g. `humanStats.ts`, exported from `src/ai/eval/index.ts`) — shared human balance-statistics extraction + `BalanceReport` packaging.
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — emit the `human` `BalanceReport` artifact for `--human`.
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — write the human balance artifact next to the recording.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — surface the shared helper's artifact from `--human`.
- `src/ai/eval/humanStats.test.ts` — pure-helper tests (single/multi-run, empty, determinism).
- CLI/tool tests — record + evaluate `--human` wiring and dev-only enforcement.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/BALANCING.md` — document the human flow + artifact.

## Related work

- **Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — parent epic; defines the shared schema and bot report.
- **Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation** (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ) — `extractBalanceStats` / `aggregateBalanceStats` / `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ) — the recording path (`npm run record`, `parseRecording`).
- **Periodically validate the human experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — downstream consumer of human balance statistics.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/BALANCING.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the dev JSONL sink record stream is the canonical human source;
  splitting on `run_header` matches `parseRecording`'s run grouping.
- **Assumption:** report `ticks`/`dt`/`sampleEveryTicks` config fields for a human
  run are derived from the recording (max tick, default dt 1/60) rather than being
  meaningful bot-config values.
- **Risk:** loading the TS core from `scripts/record-session.mjs` adds Vite SSR
  coupling to the record tool — mitigate by keeping the helper pure and the shell thin.
- **Risk — scope creep:** the `--human` same-seed comparison already delivers
  metric-level deltas; this item deliberately does **not** extend that comparison
  to the balance schema (recorded as a separate opportunity, not scope).
- **Risk:** drift between bot and human extraction paths — mitigated by
  single-helper reuse and a cross-path equivalence test.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should human balance-statistics collection be wired in? (A: `npm run record`; B: `npm run evaluate -- --human`; C: both, sharing one pure helper)" — Answer (operator): **C** — both, sharing one pure helper. Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q2: "What should the human-stats artifact look like? (A: reuse `BalanceReport` with a `human` pseudo-policy; B: dedicated `{perRun, aggregate}` artifact; C: both)" — Answer (operator): **A** — reuse the existing versioned `BalanceReport` shape via `buildBalanceReport`, byte-comparable to bot reports. Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q3: "When a recording file contains multiple human runs, what should be produced? (A: per-run + one aggregate; B: aggregate only; C: latest run only)" — Answer (operator): **A** — per-run `BalanceRunStats` for every run plus one `BalanceAggregate` across all runs, mirroring bot batches. Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN** – Screen action intensity tracking and analysis (completed)
- **AH-0MV2JT3GM001BDKG** – Documentation and full-suite verification (completed)
- **AH-0MUZJDT88002L536** – Worktree builds fail: build-audio cannot resolve the sibling ToneForge CLI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv1dluz8009ocjw, absent, acceptance, add, archetype (+109 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absent, add, archetype, balance, bot (+88 more)
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — matched: 0muy08w7y004gatz, absent, acceptance, add, aggregation (+87 more)
data.title: Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)

# HUD grey-out for zero-charge power-up rows

## Goal

When a power-up the player owns has zero available charges, render its HUD row (icon + label + value) greyed-out/inactive instead of hiding it; render normally when charges > 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a power-up the player owns has zero available charges, its HUD row is rendered greyed-out/inactive; when charges > 0 the row renders normally.
- Row visibility: an owned Phase Shift/Teleport with an empty pool stays visible (greyed), not hidden; power-ups the player has never owned stay hidden.
- The icon, label and value share one greyed styling derived from a shared grey variant (`src/powerups/icons.ts`), so icon and text cannot diverge.
- Charged rows and all non-charge rows render unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/ui/HUD.ts`: `_isPowerUpRowVisible` / `_powerUpStacks` (owned-but-empty → visible + greyed), `_addRow` grey styling, HUD docs.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts`: shared grey variant for the Phase Shift/Teleport icons used by the HUD.

## Dependencies

- Tests: HUD grey-out for empty recharge pools (test-first).
- Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence.

## Key Files

- src/ui/HUD.ts
- src/powerups/icons.ts

Audit the shipped campaign against R1–R3 and verify determinism and gym↔game parity (parent AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP, F5; covers AC4/AC5).

## Goal
Use the pure validator to audit the shipped campaign generated from defaultDifficultyCurves(), confirm no generated wave violates R1–R3 (fixed waves exempt per Q3=a), prove seeded-dynamic reproducibility, and verify gym↔game parity holds by construction.

## Context
- Build path: buildSequencedLevels(rows?, candidates?, {seed}) in src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts; campaign rows from defaultDifficultyCurves() in src/core/configStore.ts.
- Gym preview GymCurveSequencer.ts imports the same core sequencer + defaultCandidatePool, so parity holds by construction — this item must assert it (no divergent copy introduced by F2–F4).
- The difficulty error may grow where rules bind; record the before/after per-wave error for the documented campaign as part of this item.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A test audits the shipped campaign generated from defaultDifficultyCurves() using the shared validator and confirms no generated (curve/dynamic) wave violates R1–R3; fixed waves are excluded from the audit by design.
- Seeded-dynamic reproducibility is asserted: same seed yields an identical campaign; determinism is not broken by rule enforcement.
- Gym↔game parity is verified: the rules live in the shared core consumed by both the game's campaign builder and GymCurveSequencer, with no divergent rule copy (assert via the shared module/API, not source-grepping).
- Per-wave target-difficulty error growth caused by rule enforcement is measured and recorded (values referenced by F6 documentation).
- The campaign never returns empty/undeplayable and existing campaign invariant tests (campaignInvariants.test.ts, campaignRoster.test.ts) still pass.
- UK English in comments/docs.

# Reverse braking model consumes live reverse thruster values

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

Reverse braking must be gated and modelled with the live reverse values:
`asteroidsReverseEnabled` (already respected at snapshot level),
`asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` feed the
reverse forward-model instead of being absent.

As a player who re-tuned or disabled my reverse thruster, I want the bot's
reverse braking to use my configured acceleration and speed cap, so the demo
never contradicts the handling I experience.

## Scope

- Feed the live reverse acceleration and/or reverse speed cap into the reverse
  forward-model (brake distance under reverse acceleration and/or reverse
  speed cap).
- Keep the existing `mayReverse` tuning gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`,
  `reverseRetreatRange`) as tunables.
- Preserve the trouble/correction semantics from AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 (reverse
  is not a general positioning tool).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reverse forward-model consumes `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and/or `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` from the snapshot to model reverse-assisted braking distance / reverse speed cap, instead of omitting reverse physics entirely.
- Reverse remains gated on the snapshot's live `reverseEnabled`, and the existing `mayReverse` tuning gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`, `reverseRetreatRange`) remain tunables.
- The reverse-reserved-for-trouble/correction semantics of AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 are preserved (no reverse used for routine positioning).
- Unit tests cover a custom reverse config changing the reverse decision versus defaults, and reverse-disabled behaviour emitting no reverse.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `mayReverse` / reverse forward-model.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — reverse fields consumed.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — reverse gate/default docs.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts` — custom reverse config + disabled tests.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the live thruster-config snapshot child.
- Depends on the test-harness child.
- Related: AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 (reverse overuse semantics).

## Out of scope

- A full reverse-kinematics rework beyond the live numeric consumption.

## References

- Parent intake brief: AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9
- AH-0MV2JS18K006YU35 (reverse enable-flag plumbing)

# Intake Brief — Make the level/wave banner background semi-transparent and extend its duration

## Problem statement

The centred level/wave announcement banner has an opaque black background, so
during the brief pause **between levels/waves it hides the action on screen**
(carried-over asteroids keep moving, enemies are still alive). Players cannot
see what is happening behind the banner. The banner also clears too quickly to
read comfortably.

## Users

- **Player** — *"As a player, I want the level/wave banner to let me see the
  field behind it while I read the announcement, and to stay on screen long
  enough to read."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The level/wave banner background is **60 % opaque** (alpha ≈ `0.6`) instead
   of fully opaque, for both the level-start announcement and the
   wave-transition banner.
2. The banner stays visible for **3.5 s** (current 1.5 s + 2 s) for both the
   level-start announcement and the wave-transition banner, then hides
   automatically as before.
3. Both the background alpha and the duration are exported constants (e.g.
   `BANNER_BACKGROUND_ALPHA`, `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS`) so tests can pin
   them.
4. Existing tests that assert the old 1.5–2 s hide timing
   (`AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN AC1/AC2`, `AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV AC6`) are updated to
   the new 3.5 s window, and a test asserts the semi-transparent background.
5. GDD §3 (level-progression transient-banner wording) is updated to the new
   3.5 s window; the constant's doc comment no longer claims the ~1.5–2 s
   requirement.
6. The full project test suite passes with the changes (no dead
   constants/parameters left behind).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** the banner exists **only** in `PlayScene` (no gym
  renders it), so no gym-scene change is required.
- **Readability:** the semi-transparent background must keep the white banner
  text legible against gameplay; at 60 % the existing 34 px monospace text with
  `padding {x: 20, y: 12}` is unchanged.
- The banner must remain **transient** — it still expires on its own (just
  after 3.5 s), per the GDD's "transient transitions" principle
  (AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN).
- Phaser `TextStyle.backgroundColor` takes a CSS colour string; alpha must be
  expressed as `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` (verify it renders in Phaser 4.2.1 — if
  unsupported in the canvas fill path, use `setBackgroundColor('rgba(...)')`
  or a `Graphics` rectangle behind the text).

## Existing state

- `BANNER_STYLE` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:338`) sets
  `backgroundColor: '#000000'` — fully opaque.
- `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS = 1.5` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:301`); its doc
  comment says the value "must be within the ~1.5–2 s window required by
  AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN" — this changes to 3.5 s.
- The level-start announcement (`_announceLevel`) and the wave-transition
  banner (`_updateTransitionBanner`) both call the shared `_showBanner`, so a
  single duration/alpha change covers both surfaces.

## Desired change

- Set `backgroundColor: 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)'` in `BANNER_STYLE` (or the
  equivalent alpha-based background) so the field remains visible.
- Raise `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` to `3.5` and update its doc comment to drop
  the old ~1.5–2 s constraint.
- Update the existing banner-timing tests to the new window and add a test
  pinning the semi-transparent background.
- Update GDD §3 wording for the new banner window.

## Acceptance-criteria coverage of existing tests

The following existing tests hard-code the old 2 s hide window and must be
updated with this change:
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` `AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN AC1` (`tick(2.0)` →
  hidden) and `AC2` (reappears + hides again).
- `AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV AC6` "level-name banner remains transient" (`tick` at
  2 s / 2 s + 0.5 s expect visible-then-hidden).

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `BANNER_STYLE` background and
  `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` (+ doc comment).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — update banner-timing tests; add
  semi-transparent-background assertion.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §3 transient-banner wording for the new
  3.5 s window.

## Related work

- AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN — "Level transition banner persists for the whole wave"
  (established the transient ~1.5–2 s hide behaviour this item extends).
- AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV — "Show the level name in the level-start banner"
  (banner content/transience tests this item must keep passing).
- AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2 — "Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K'"
  (established the banner label text).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2** – Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K' (completed)
- **AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN** – Level transition banner persists for the whole wave (completed)
- **AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV** – Show the level name in the level-start banner (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: also, background, banner, hard, level (+11 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: also, banner, hard, level, levels (+9 more)
- `README.md` — matched: also, background, hard, level, levels (+9 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "visible for 2 seconds longer" means the current 1.5 s
  duration is increased **to 3.5 s** (1.5 + 2). If the intent was a 2 s total,
  only the constant and GDD wording change — flag before implementation.
- **Risk (medium):** Phaser 4.2.1 `TextStyle.backgroundColor` support for
  `rgba()` CSS strings must be verified; fallback is a `Graphics` rectangle
  behind the text or `setBackgroundColor('rgba(0,0,0,0.6)')`. Covered by the
  automated background assertion in AC4.
- **Risk (low):** extending the banner window to 3.5 s lengthens the time the
  centred text covers the playfield; the 60 % transparency (not full removal)
  keeps the field visible while retaining the GDD "transient" principle.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no follow-up opportunities were observed during
  intake; if a larger banner redesign (animation, fade, resizing) is requested
  later, it should be tracked as a separate work item, not folded in here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How transparent should the banner background be?" — Answer
  (operator): "60 % opacity". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Should the +2 s apply to both the level-start announcement and the
  wave-transition banner?" — Answer (operator): "Both". Source: interactive
  reply. Note: both surfaces share `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` via `_showBanner`,
  so a single constant change covers both.
- Q3: "How should the GDD §3 '~1.5–2 s transient' wording be handled?" —
  Answer (operator): "Update GDD". Source: interactive reply.
- Research summary: inspected `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`BANNER_STYLE`,
  `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS`, `_showBanner`) and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
  banner tests; `wl search "banner"` surfaced the related items above. No gym
  scene renders the banner (gym-parity check performed). Phaser version is
  4.2.1; `rgba()` in `TextStyle.backgroundColor` to be verified at
  implementation time (constraint noted).

# Intake brief — Smart Bomb is too powerful

## Problem statement

The Smart Bomb power-up (Defender homage, AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ) is too strong: a hold-full reward makes its screen-wide pulse repeat every **5 seconds** at base level (and up to every 2 s at the cap), and its pulse radius (1200 → 2400 px) already exceeds the whole 960×540 play field from the first pickup. The result is a near-continuous screen clear that trivialises every wave the moment the permanent smart bomb is earned.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the smart bomb to stay a tense "panic button" (rare, high-value wake-up) rather than a passive auto-win.

**User story:** "As a player who earned the permanent smart bomb from the hold-full choice, I want it to pulse rarely (once every ~30 seconds at first, never more often than once per 10 seconds) and to cover only a modest area around my ship, so the game stays challenging instead of auto-playing."

## Desired change

1. **Pulse rate (permanent smart bomb only):** fire every `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` seconds — 30 s on the first grant (level 0), −2 s per further level, floor 10 s. A field pickup (one-shot) still fires exactly once on collection.
2. **Pulse radius (both permanent and runtime-collected):** base = **200 px** (10 × `SHIP_SIZE` = 10 × 20), additive **+2 % of base per level** → `min(400, 200 × (1 + 0.02 × level))`, capped at 400 px (2× base). No longer screen-wide.
3. **Damage unchanged:** stays 1 → 3 HP per pulse (no change).
4. Resolved through the same shared `AoEDescriptor`/`screenPulse` seam so the game and every gym run identical code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A permanent smart bomb pulses on the interval `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` seconds: 30 s at level 0 (first grant), 28 s at level 1, … 10 s at level 10 and beyond; `smartBombInterval()` reflects this schedule.
- The smart bomb pulse radius resolves to `min(400, 200 × (1 + 0.02 × level))` px: 200 px base (10× ship size), additive +2 % of base per level, capped at 400 px. Applies to both permanent pulses and one-shot field pickups.
- Smart bomb damage per pulse is unchanged (1 → 3 HP across levels).
- Behaviour lands in the shared core (`effects.ts` / `powerUpLevels.ts` + the AoE seam) so `PlayScene` and the gym scenes (`GymPowerUpsCombat` and the shared `powerUpLeveling.parity` tests) run identical code — no divergent copies.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular, "screen-wide" descriptions of the pulse must be corrected in `docs/Game Design Document.md` and `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` (§6).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (including updated `powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `effects.test.ts` and `AoeWeapons.test.ts` assertions that pin the old 1200/2400 px and 0.2→0.5/s values).

## Constraints

- The level model in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` currently stores every variable on the `exponential-saturation` curve (`src/utils/curve.ts`; the `UpgradeCurve` union has a single member). The two new schedules — linear-descending interval and linear-additive radius — are **not expressible** by that curve, so a new curve type (e.g. a linear/clamped variant) must be added to `src/utils/curve.ts` and consumed by the smart-bomb specs. Keep the resolver pure, deterministic, monotonic and clamped as today.
- The pulse-frequency axis is stored non-decreasing (`smartBombFrequency`, pulses/s); the desired *interval* schedule is descending, so represent the change as `frequency = 1 / max(10, 30 − 2×level)` (non-decreasing, meets the model's monotonicity contract) or restructure the variable — implementation choice, but `smartBombInterval()` must return the documented schedule.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): the change must be applied once in the shared core and consumed by both sides; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard in `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` enforces this.
- `SHIP_SIZE = 20` (`src/core/constants.ts`) is the ship-size base used by the magnet convention (`magnetRadius`), and 10× of it = **200 px** (operator decision Q1-A).

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.smart_bomb`: `aoeRadius` base 1200/cap 2400 (k=0.3, exponential-saturation), `smartBombDamage` base 1/cap 3, `smartBombFrequency` base 0.2/cap 0.5 (k=0.3).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `isSmartBombPermanent()`, `smartBombFrequency()`, `smartBombInterval()`, `smartBombAoe()`, `updateSmartBomb(dt)`; permanent pulse timer.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_updateSmartBomb(dt)` consumes `smartBombAoe()` and applies it through the shared AoE seam; `CombatScene.onSmartBombPulse`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `SHIP_SIZE = 20`.
- Tests pinning current values: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` (102–107, 136–163), `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (~596–656), `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` (~810–866).

## Key Files

- `src/utils/curve.ts` — new linear/clamped curve type (currently only `exponential-saturation`).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — re-spec the three smart-bomb variables (radius schedule, frequency/interval schedule; damage unchanged) with the new curve.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `smartBombInterval()` / `smartBombAoe()` resolve the new schedules; comments updated.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — only if the seam needs adjustment (expected: none).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — possibly a named constant for the 10× ship-size / 2 % tuning knobs.
- Tests: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

## Related work

- AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ — Defender smart bomb pulse (the original feature being re-balanced; completed).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — Design level curves for all power-ups (the model this change extends).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention (must be preserved).
- AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4 — Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch (adjacent pickup behaviour; completed).
- AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4 / AH-0MV1BIUGE005BJO8 — classic power-up research epics that introduced the smart bomb (background).

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ** – Defender smart bomb pulse (completed)
- **AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4** – Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch (completed)
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `README.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`

## Risks & assumptions

- **Curve-family extension risk:** adding a linear/clamped curve to `src/utils/curve.ts` touches shared machinery used by all levelled variables — the new curve must stay pure/deterministic and unit-tested so it cannot regress weapon or other power-up curves. Mitigation: new curve type is additive; existing specs keep `exponential-saturation`; parity/equivalence tests guard the seam.
- **Value-inversion risk:** switching the smart-bomb axis meaning (interval vs frequency) could break `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` / hold-full overlay deltas or the monotonicity contract — keep frequency non-decreasing (`1/interval`) and clamp, and pin expected resolved values in `powerUpLevels.test.ts`.
- **Scope creep:** opportunities observed during implementation (e.g. retuning the *Bomb* power-up, smart bomb visual redesign for a smaller radius) must be recorded as linked work items, not absorbed into this item.

## Assumptions

- "lvl1" in the request maps to **level 0** (first collection) in the code's level semantics — i.e. the base schedule is 30 s and the basic radius is 200 px at first pickup.
- Interval applies only to the *permanent* (hold-full) smart bomb; the one-shot field pickup fires once regardless.
- Damage tuning (1 → 3) is out of scope for this change.
- Radius cap of 2× base (400 px) is acceptable (operator decision Q2-A); radius growth is **additive** (+2 % of base per level).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "10× the radius of the ship: what is the base radius?" — Answer (operator): **A — 10 × SHIP_SIZE = 200 px**, matching the magnet/scoop "× ship size" convention (`magnetRadius` uses `shipSize` as the base unit). Source: interactive reply to intake round 1. Research: `src/core/constants.ts` `SHIP_SIZE = 20`; `src/powerups/effects.ts` `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)`.
- Q2: "2 % every lvl: additive or compound, and cap?" — Answer (operator): **A — additive** `base × (1 + 0.02 × level)`, **cap 2× base = 400 px**. Source: interactive reply. Research: current `powerUpLevels.ts` variables are monotonic non-decreasing with infinite level space, so a finite cap is required by the model's clamping contract.
- Q3: "Confirm interval schedule `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` with level 0 = first pickup, and damage unchanged?" — Answer (operator): **Confirmed.** Source: interactive reply. Research: `effects.ts` `updateSmartBomb`/`smartBombInterval` (permanent only); field pickup path is one-shot.

# Stop ignoring standups/ so the standup skill can version report history

## Problem

The standup skill (global) auto-commits and pushes each generated daily report so standup history is versioned. It uses a surgical git add of only the report file followed by commit and push.

In this repo standups/ is ignored in two places:

- .gitignore line ~50: standups/ under the comment "Generated daily standup reports (automated artefacts, never committed)"
- .git/info/exclude: a machine-local entry added as a bootstrap until .gitignore lands on dev

Because the path is ignored, git add silently skips the report file and the script's commit becomes a silent no-op — standup history is never versioned. Observed 14th Oct 2026: standups/2026_10_14.md was written but the commit failed with "The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: standups".

## Background / conflicting prior decision

AH-0MU480XW8009160C (completed, v0.1.4, commit 0cd5984) deliberately added the .gitignore entry to stop generated reports dirtying the working tree, which blocked the implement skill's dirty-tree gate. Since then the standup skill moved to the auto-commit strategy: reports are created once per day and committed immediately, so the tree-cleanliness concern no longer applies to the standalone report files. The skill docs explicitly identify the ignore as a stopgap that makes the commit a silent no-op (SA-0MUDYRHVZ005PQP4).

## Scope

In scope:
- Remove the standups/ entry (and its explanatory comment) from .gitignore.
- Remove the standups/ entry from the machine-local .git/info/exclude.
- Backfill history: commit the existing generated reports already on disk so the versioned standup history starts now.
- Re-run the standup script to confirm the commit-and-push path now works.

Out of scope: changing how/when the standup report is generated; touching other repos' ignore rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: standups/ no longer appears in .gitignore or .git/info/exclude.
- [ ] AC2: Existing report files on disk are tracked in git and pushed to dev.
- [ ] AC3: Re-running the standup generator commits and pushes the report (no "paths are ignored" warning).
- [ ] AC4: git status --porcelain is clean after the generator run (no stray dirty state introduced).
- [ ] AC5: All tests pass (npm test).
